about.heroSubtitle: A story about food, family, and thirty plants a week.
about.story1: My grandfather had a grocery store in Tongelre, Eindhoven. Before the store, he had a horse and cart, riding through the neighbourhood, selling fruits and vegetables door to door. Eventually the cart became a shop. My mother grew up working there. My uncles did too. By the time my uncle took over and moved to a busier street, I had just been born. There is a photo of me, days old, lying between the fruit on the counter.
about.story2: Growing up, I was always around. Piling empty crates, loading the van for wholesale runs, learning which tomatoes were ripe. As I got older I started cooking, preparing dishes to sell in the store, and somewhere along the way that turned into a genuine love. I still cook every day, still experiment, still taste everything.
about.discovery1: About two years ago, my girlfriend and I watched a gut health documentary on Netflix. The message was surprising: it's not about eating the right foods more often, it's about eating a wide variety of plants. As many different ones as possible.
about.discovery2: The science made sense. Thousands of years ago we ate whatever we could find, roots, berries, seeds, leaves, everything the land offered. That variety fed an entire ecosystem of bacteria in the gut. Different bacteria for different plants. Together, they create balance. Modern diets, heavy on processed food, bread, meat, and sugar, have narrowed that variety dramatically. Researchers now suggest a simple target: 30 different plants per week. Fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, herbs, and spices all count.
about.callout: 30 plants a week. Backed by science, made into a game.
about.appTitle: It should be easier. And more fun.
about.app1: We took the challenge seriously. Two years later, I was still tracking plants in a notes app and on scraps of paper, and I thought: there should be a better way. What if there was an app that tracked your variety for you, told you which plants you were missing, and gave you inspiration for next week's shopping? What if you could challenge friends and family to eat more diverse, and actually make a game of it?
about.vision1: Project Food isn't about eating perfectly. It's about eating curiously, exploring vegetables you've never tried, adding a new herb to your list, building a habit that makes you feel genuinely good. Whether you grew up between the vegetables or you're just discovering them, there's always more to explore.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Project Food is a family app. A parent logs which plants the family tasted at dinner, and the kids collect cards and stamps. This policy explains what we store, why, who helps us run the service and how you delete everything. It applies to the Project Food app and to projectfood.dev.

sections.title: 1. Who we are
sections.body: Project Food is the data controller for the data described here. It is run from the Netherlands. For anything privacy related, write to info@projectfood.dev.

sections.title: 2. Made for families, used by parents
sections.intro: Only adults create an account and sign in. Children never sign in, never get email or notifications from us and cannot be contacted through the app.
items: A parent adds each family member as a profile: a first name or nickname, and whether they are a child or an adult. That is all we ask. No birth dates, surnames or photos.
The parent decides what is entered, can rename or remove a profile at any time, and removes everything by deleting the account.
Children's profiles are never used for advertising or profiling and are never shared with other families.

sections.title: 3. What we store
sections.intro: When you use the app we store:
items: Account: your email address, and your name and profile picture if you sign in with Google or Apple. Sign-in codes go to your email.
Household: the family name, dinner time, time zone and language.
Family members: first name or nickname, child or adult, a colour, and an avatar chosen from our set.
Tastes: which plants each member tasted on which day, and what that unlocks (cards, stamps, the family streak).

Notifications: whether you allowed push notifications, your preferences, a device push token, and per message whether it was delivered, opened and followed by a log within three hours. We use this to stop nudging a family that ignores us.
Product events: a small set of in-app events such as a plant logged, onboarding completed or a survey submitted, tied to your account. No advertising identifiers, no tracking across apps.
Optional: survey answers and plant suggestions, if you submit them.
Technical logs kept by our hosting providers (IP address, device type, timestamps) to keep the service secure.

sections.title: 4. What we never do
items: No advertising in the app and no ad networks.
No selling, renting or trading of personal data.
No profiling of children and no sharing of family data with other families.
No third-party analytics or tracking SDKs inside the app.

sections.title: 5. Why we may process it
sections.intro: Under the GDPR we rely on:
items: Contract (Art. 6(1)(b)): to provide the app you signed up for, including the family profiles you create.
Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): for push notifications and the optional survey. You can withdraw it at any time in the app or in your phone settings.
Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)): to keep the service secure and to see, through the few product events above, whether the app works.
sections.outro: Children's profiles are processed on the parent's instruction, as part of the parent's account. Project Food does not collect data from children itself.

sections.title: 6. Notifications
sections.intro: The app asks for push permission while you set up your family, right where you choose the dinner time, and you can say no. If you skip it, we ask once more after your first log, and after that only when you turn it on in Account → Notifications.
items: Essential: the dinner question and the streak keeper. On by default once you allow notifications.
Tips & news: card and stamp teasers and the Sunday nudge. Off by default.
Turn each kind off in Account → Notifications, or all of them in your phone settings. If three messages in a row are ignored, we stay quiet for a week.
sections.outro: Messages travel through Expo's push service and Apple's or Google's notification services, which receive the device token and the message text.

sections.title: 7. Who helps us run the service
sections.intro: We use these processors, each under a data processing agreement or standard contractual clauses:
items: Supabase: database, sign-in and server functions, hosted in the EU (Ireland).
Vercel: hosting of projectfood.dev (USA).
Expo (EAS): app builds, updates and the push notification relay (USA).
Google: Google sign-in, Android push delivery (Firebase Cloud Messaging) and the mailbox behind info@projectfood.dev (Google Workspace).
Apple: Sign in with Apple and iOS push delivery.
Resend: sign-in codes and contact-form email (USA).

sections.title: 8. Retention and deletion
sections.intro: We keep your data for as long as your account exists. You delete it yourself:
items: In the app: Account → Delete account.
On the web: the delete-account page linked below, with a code sent to your email.
sections.outro: Deleting removes your account, the household you created with its member profiles, cards and stamps, notification history and push tokens, immediately. The tastes themselves stay as anonymous statistics: which plant on which day, under random ids that no longer link to any person or family. Database backups expire within 30 days. If you joined a household created by another parent, that household and its tastes stay with them; only your account and sign-in go.
sections.linkLabel: Delete your account on the web

sections.title: 9. Your rights
items: Access: ask for a copy of the data we hold about you (Art. 15).
Rectification: correct inaccurate or incomplete data (Art. 16).
Erasure: delete your account and everything in it (Art. 17).
Portability: receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format (Art. 20).
Restriction and objection: limit or object to how we process your data (Art. 18, 21).
Withdraw consent: for notifications and the survey, at any time.
sections.outro: Write to info@projectfood.dev. If you think we have handled your data wrongly, you can complain to the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl).

sections.title: 10. Cookies
sections.body: The app uses no cookies. The website uses one functional cookie, pf_locale, which remembers your language for a year and needs no consent. The website uses Vercel's privacy-friendly analytics, which set no cookies and do not identify you.

sections.title: 11. Security
sections.body: Data travels encrypted (TLS) and is stored with row-level security, so each household can only reach its own data. Access to the database is limited to the founder. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach ever affects your data we will tell you and the authority as the law requires.

sections.title: 12. Changes
sections.body: When this policy changes we update the date at the top. For significant changes we tell you in the app or by email before they take effect.

deleteAccount.title: Delete your account
deleteAccount.intro: Deleting removes your account, the household you created with its member profiles, cards and stamps, notification history and push tokens. Your tastes stay only as anonymous statistics: which plant on which day, linked to no one. It cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.inAppBody: Open Account → Delete account. That is the quickest way.
deleteAccount.webBody: Enter the email address of your account. We send a code to that address; enter it, then confirm.
deleteAccount.codeSent: If this address has a Project Food account, a code is on its way. Check your inbox and your spam folder.
deleteAccount.confirmBody: Delete the account for {email} and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.doneBody: Your account and its data are gone. Thank you for having been at the table.
deleteAccount.errorCode: That code did not work. Request a new one and try again.
deleteAccount.errorDelete: Something went wrong. Please try again, or write to info@projectfood.dev from the address of your account.
deleteAccount.fallback: No access to that email any more? Write to info@projectfood.dev and we handle it by hand within 30 days.
deleteAccount.joined: If you joined a household that another parent created, that household stays with them.
